[size=150][b]Lionheart Fixt 0.23.0 - What the Crescent Is Worth[/b][/size]

Act 8 is the Knights of Saladin's own country. The Assassins of Alamut twice sent knives into Saladin's
tent; the Old Man is the reason that order exists in this story. And choosing it bought less in that
desert than choosing any other faction.

The count: [i]Templar IS[/i] 13 checks, [i]Inquisitor IS[/i] 12, Goblin Champion 4, [b][i]Saladin IS[/i] 6[/b] -- and three
of those six were a single greeting selector. The Knight of Saladin who meets you in the dunes is handed
to everybody. Being one of his order bought you a salutation.

[b]The ladder nobody read[/b]

Every order in this game has a three-rung ladder. Each rung is a faction that permanently grants
modifiers [b]and a point of rank[/b], so the rank counts how many promotions you took:

| | Saladin | how you get it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Aswaran | the Dream Djinni trials |
| 2 | Blessed | Jafar, on taking the Montaillou or Montserrat errand |
| 3 | [b]Exalted[/b] | all five green Way Crystals |

Exalted is the strongest faction perk in the game: +13 one-handed, +13 two-handed, +12 Turn Undead, +5%
crushing, +5% slashing, +20 carry. Reaching it means the initiation, the errand and the crystal hunt --
three long arcs across four acts.

[i]Saladin Highlevel[/i] is the canned requirement that tests for it, exactly as [i]Goblin Horde Highlevel[/i] tests
the Horde's. [b]It is referenced by nothing in the shipped game.[/b] Neither is [i]Templar Favored[/i],
[i]Templar Highlevel[/i], [i]Inquisitor Favored[/i] or [i]Inquisitor Highlevel[/i]. The only faction ladder anything in
Lionheart reads is the Goblin Horde's -- and that is this project's own work, from 0.1.0.

The asymmetry shows worst at the Old Man himself, who answers a Goblin Champion by rank -- *"The Great
Khan sent proud warriors after you once and not one of them came home. The Horde calls me Champion now."*
-- and answered the highest-ranking knight of the order whose Sultan he twice tried to murder with the
same line he gives a week-old initiate.

[b]Act 8 reads it now[/b]

The knight at the dunes greets an Exalted as a superior rather than a comrade, and will tell one what the
order does not say in its chapter houses:

[i]*"The order does not speak of Alamut in the chapter houses, so I will speak of it here, in the sand,[/i]
[i]where there is nobody to be shocked. Every Aswaran is told one thing on the day of the oath and never[/i]
[i]told it again: if the Old Man moves against the Sultan's house a third time, the highest of us who is[/i]
[i]nearest rides, and does not wait for permission, and does not come back with prisoners. In eighty years[/i]
[i]nobody has ever been nearest. You are nearest."*[/i]

The Old Man gets a line for the rank, beside the one he already had for the Horde's.

[b]And the order rides[/b]

The reason the rank could not easily be worth more than a greeting turned out to be the finding: [b]the
Knight of Saladin exists on exactly one map.[/b] [i]02 Shifting Dunes[/i] names him eleven times; the seven maps
past it name him zero. He says *"my sword is yours"*, walks you to the door of the fortress, and stops
there for the rest of the game.

An Exalted can now tell him to come the whole way in, and he does - through the Maw of the Assassin, the
Acid Wash, the Chamber of Torment and the Dark Temple. He stops at the door of the Old Man's chamber,
which is both the safer choice and the better reading of the oath he quoted: somebody has to be outside it
to be sure that nobody comes back with prisoners.

[b]Two more things in the same desert[/b]

[b]The merchant.[/b] He is the most expensive shop in the game -- a price multiplier of 2, where the next
worst is 1.7 and the median is 1. He now recognises the order and takes half a point off it, stacking
with his haggling, so a knight who also haggles pays 1.3 where everyone else pays 1.8. And he stocks
[b]Great, Superior and Supreme Healing[/b] -- the three potion tiers 0.4.0 unlocked through the herbalist's
errands, which until now existed only in Barcelona, seven acts behind you.

[b]The bird men.[/b] Fazeem's encounter is a confidence trick: hear about them from the merchant, pass Speech
70 to claim you know secrets about rain, Barter to be paid for them, then Intelligence 6 to invent the
detail that does the work -- that the blood of an Assassin makes rain. They believe it and go hunting
Assassins for you. There is no other way out; thirty gold buys you off, and every other reply, *"I think
I'll be going now"* included, starts the fight.

A knight of the order does not need the lie. He is in that desert to kill Assassins and they are being
robbed by Assassins, and that is not a con, it is a shared enemy:

[i]*"Knife. Men. Wear. Black. Take. Our. Eggs. Take. Our. Water. Take. Our. Young. For. Sport. You. Hunt.[/i]
[i]Them? True? Lie. And. We. Eat. You. Now."*[/i]

It reaches the same bargain the con reaches. It costs the money the con earns, because the con is a sale
and this is not. Four gates skipped, one payment forgone.

[b]Fixt[/b] is a cumulative restoration-and-repair mod for Lionheart, after Fallout Fixt.

Download, unzip, run [i]Mod Manager.bat[/i]. Needs a character who has [b]not yet entered the Alamut maps[/b] --
new map parts do not appear on a save that has already visited a level. The rank content needs a Knight of
Saladin who took all three promotions; the merchant and the bird men need only a knight of any rank.
Unplayed; what you find goes into 0.23.1.

https://github.com/EricHype/LionheartFixt/releases/tag/v0.23.0
